pages.promptText:
CPH-F-I6-FLASH-SHADOW
The first line is a prompt identifier only. Never render it as text in the image.

Professional high-end fashion photography, shot on set on location with a professional model who is styled and directed. Vertical 3:4, a portrait-format magazine page, one continuous photograph filling the frame edge to edge.

REFERENCES: Generate an image using the EXACT model appearance from the provided model reference images. The face close-up is provided — reproduce the face, facial features, expression, AND MAKEUP with maximum accuracy. Face and skin tone must match exactly. Her hair is styled as written below, not as in the face photo. The headless outfit photo shows how the outfit is worn together. The product photos define each garment's exact colour and construction; take only the named garment from each. The location photo defines the real place, not the viewpoint, the weather, the time of day or the people.

THE MODEL: a professional fashion model, about 30, 175 cm, slim high-fashion build, real human limb lengths. Her dark brown hair is slicked straight back from her forehead with a wet-look gel, close to the head, both ears showing, the lengths falling behind her shoulders in damp strands; no fringe, no loose hair on her face. Real skin with light natural freckles, bare-looking makeup.

OUTFIT, exactly as the product photos, nothing added:
- CLANE check shaggy hand-knit top: camel beige, a long shaggy brushed pile with a faint checked pattern in the knit, a crew neck, a boxy slightly cropped shape, long wide sleeves. Its hem is worn OUT over the skirt. No bare skin at the waist.
- CLANE satin straight maxi skirt: pale champagne beige satin with a soft sheen, a narrow straight shape falling to the ankles, moving softly.
- CLANE side-cut stacked flat shoes: ivory white smooth leather, a deep V cut at the sides, a low stacked heel.
- Grey socks, only a sliver showing at the ankle.
No bag, no jewellery, no scarf, no hat, no other accessories. Her hands are empty.

PLACE: outdoors on the harbour front in Copenhagen, as in the location photo: the Royal Playhouse, a long low building of dark smoked brick under a band of tall green-tinted glass, standing on a wide promenade of weathered pale oak planks raised over the harbour water on piers. No trees, no branches, no leaves inside the frame. No other people near her, no signs, no readable text, no logos, no flags, no boats with writing.

SHOT: i-D STYLE, HARSH DIRECT FLASH, HARD SHADOW. Her whole figure from the top of her head to her shoes is in the frame. Camera at her waist height, close, a 28mm lens: she stands right in front of the dark smoked-brick wall, about half a metre from it; the raw on-camera flash fired from just above the lens throws a crisp, hard black shadow of her whole outline onto the brick right behind her and a little to one side, a second dark figure on the wall. One real photograph taken at this place in Copenhagen, never a figure pasted in front of a backdrop: she and the ground share one light and one direction of shadow.

ACTION: She stands with her body turned slightly to one side, her weight on one hip and that knee soft, both hands deep in the pockets of the long champagne satin skirt or hanging loose; the shaggy camel knit bright in the flash, the satin skirt catching hard highlights.

ATTITUDE: she owns the place and nothing here impresses her. Her body is settled and takes up room: weight in one hip, shoulders low, chest open, an easy wide stance or a long stride. Hands are quiet, in a pocket, on the bag or hanging. She never bends toward anything; when she looks at something below her, only her eyes go down.

FACE: Emotionless, eternal beauty — a face that reveals nothing, like a sculpture. She looks straight into the lens, flat and unbothered, the flash catching sharp highlights in her eyes. No smile.

LIGHT: soft, bright northern-European midday light under a thin high haze, gentle shadows; the oak planks are pale silver-gold. The same light lies on her and on the wood. Lit by a direct on-camera flash from the front, overpowering the daylight on her; the place behind her a stop darker.

LENS AND FILM: i-D magazine street editorial. Shot on a compact 35mm film camera with an on-camera DIRECT FLASH fired straight at her from the front, even in daylight: her face and clothes are hard-lit and bright with a crisp flash shadow just behind her, while the place behind her falls a stop darker. Kodak Portra 800, visible grain, punchy natural colour, slight flash falloff at the edges. Raw, immediate, a little off-balance, never polished catalogue lighting. No cut-out edge, no digital sharpening.

NEVER: a bowed head, a polite catalogue stance, a bag, added text or logos, readable signs, written characters, watermarks, borders, camera equipment, a second bag, changed garments, a rounder or younger face, a smile, closed eyes, an elongated body, hands touching hair or face, a rear view, a full profile, bare skin at the waist, a coat worn over the shoulders without the arms in the sleeves, crowds, people close to her, a rear view, her back to the camera, trees, leaves, other people, a wide stance, legs apart, arms crossed, other people.

CPH-F-I6-FLASH-SHADOW
